items.item_text: 01. Do you have a Master’s degree in counseling, social work, rehabilitation counseling, guidance counseling, educational counseling, or career development, or the equivalent, and have two years of occupational experience in work relating to justice impacted populations or a related disproportionate impacted (DI) group? Options: Yes | No

02. If you answer No above, please describe your education/experience to be consider for the equivalency for the position. If you answered Yes to the previous question, please type N/A into the text box.

Master’s degree in counseling, social work, rehabilitation counseling, guidance counseling, educational counseling, or career development, or the equivalent, and shall have two years of occupational experience in work relating to justice impacted populations or a related disproportionate impacted (DI) group.
Experience connecting students to necessary resources both on and off-campus within the community, such as housing referrals, food insecurities, mental health issues, etc.
Experience working with Justice Scholars or similar programs focused on justice-involved teens/adults.
Experience understanding and trained in trauma-informed frame-works.
Experience working with justice-involved populations, in higher education, and/or in custodial or alternative education settings is preferred.
Academic counseling in juvenile detention facilities. Education programs and services that are designed to support incarcerated and formerly incarcerated students.
Understanding of the needs, barriers, and strengths of incarcerated, formerly incarcerated, and system-impacted student populations.
Best practices in serving the unique needs of incarcerated and formerly incarcerated students, including conditions of probation.
An understanding of and sensitivity to meeting the needs of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability and ethnic background of the student, community, and employee population
Knowledge of student support services, retention strategies, and educational pathways in community colleges.
Working knowledge of instructional support practices, mentoring, tutoring, and student engagement strategies.
Familiarity with or ability to learn policies and procedures related to education in juvenile detention facilities.
Strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills with demonstrated cultural humility and sensitivity to diverse populations.
Ability to maintain accurate records, collect data, and support program reporting efforts.
Ability to work effectively in both custodial (juvenile hall) and campus-based environments. Ability to support faculty and students in instructional settings.
Ability to build rapport and trust with justice-involved students.
Ability to coordinate multiple tasks, prioritize responsibilities, and meet program timelines.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when working with sensitive student information.
